findings.title: A MEMBER's `*` broadcast includes the sender's own roster row, and a member can message its own roster id — the tool hands the resolver the SESSION id while roster targets are M-ids
findings.where: packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/index.ts · the `agent_teams_mail` send branch (`resolveRecipients({ ..., selfId: callerId })` and `fromMemberId: ownMember.id`); packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/mailbox-store.ts · sendMany (the self guard compares `target.id === input.fromId` only)
findings.what: For a member caller the directory mixes two id spaces: `selfId` is the session id (`callerId`), while `members` are roster ids (`M1`). Probe S19 resolves `*` to [M1, M2, lead-session] for a caller whose own roster row IS M1; S20 writes all three rows. S21 sends to the caller's own roster id and returns `ok: true` (the store's self check never fires because target.id 'M1' ≠ fromId 'session-M1'). The lead caller is unaffected (its session id IS the lead id), and the shipped tool arm only broadcasts AS THE LEAD, which is why the suite is green.
findings.why: Contract §5 says `"*"` is a fan-out to every member plus the lead, EXCLUDING THE SENDER, and the mailbox's own rule is that a member cannot message itself (the store test pins it at the store seam). At the tool seam both rules are defeated for members because the roster id and the session id are different strings — exactly the D16c class the same file documents. Effects: a member's broadcast mints a self-addressed row (its own inbox grows, its summary counts it, and a cell/team view renders it as a message it sent to itself).
findings.direction: Pass the caller's own ROSTER id as the resolver's `selfId` (`ownMember?.id ?? callerId`) and compare the target against BOTH `input.fromId` and `input.fromMemberId` in sendMany's self guard. Add a tool-level arm for a MEMBER's `*` (and a member's self-send) — the lead-only arm cannot see this seam. Small, local change in T2's two files.

findings.title: The wake-failure record is a PROCESS log line, while §5 says 'recorded with a reason, exactly like today's cellwork captain path' — and the code comment claims that equivalence
findings.where: packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/index.ts · the delivery loop (`rowLogLine(... the transport refused it ...)`)
findings.what: For a lead recipient (and any member with no handle) the row stays durable and undelivered, but the failure is only `rowLogLine` — the cellwork captain path records a durable `wake` record with one of four reasons. The inline comment says 'recorded with the reason here, exactly like the cellwork captain path (contract §5)', which overstates what the code does.
findings.why: A process log line is not readable from the mailbox, so an operator diagnosing 'the lead never woke' has no durable reason on this plane. The Lead declared the log-line behaviour an accepted bound; the mismatch that remains is the comment and PR-body honesty, not the behaviour.
findings.direction: Either write a durable wake outcome (reason) beside the row, or amend §5/§12 to declare the log-line bound AND soften the comment so it does not claim cellwork parity. Record it with the other accepted bounds in §12.

findings.title: The team mailbox's `fold` wrapper DROPS the protocol fold's problem list, so duplicated ids / unresolved references are invisible on this plane
findings.what: Probe S22: a log with two `send` rows sharing `d1` folds to ONE message (first write wins, correct) and the wrapper exposes only `{ messages }` — no problems. The protocol fold reported the duplicate; the team plane never surfaces it. The same wrapper re-reads stamps from the raw lines and lets the LAST duplicate's `cellId`/`fromCell` ride the FIRST message's body.
findings.why: The unified store is exactly where a second writer (cellwork) begins appending, so a duplicate id is the one anomaly an operator most needs to see; silently keeping the first write is tolerable, silently hiding it is not. The web projection and the mail tool both read through this wrapper, so no surface reports it.
findings.direction: Expose `problems` on `MailboxState` (or log them with the mailbox path) and keep the stamps first-wins to match the content policy. Non-blocking for this wave.
findings.evidence: probes.ts S22 in output.log; protocol fold contract I8

findings.title: AC-8's test asserts only 3 of the 5 envelope fields the projection carries
findings.what: The projection carries `kind`, `threadId`, `replyTo`, `question`, `answer` and `readBy` (probe S23 proves all of them), but the shipped arm asserts only `kind`, `threadId` and `question.questionId/options` — no `replyTo` and no `answer` assertion.
findings.why: AC-8 says the projection carries the new fields 'and its test asserts them'; a future edit could drop `replyTo`/`answer` from the projection and the suite would stay green.
findings.direction: Append one `answer` row with `replyTo` and assert both fields in the same arm.
